text:
You who think I do not believe
when we argue, the two of us,
do not imagine my desire,
my thirst, my hunger for God;


nor have you heard my cry
of despair, which fills
the entrails of darkness
invoking the Infinite;


nor do you see my thought,
which, bent on producing
an ideal, often suffers
the tortures of childbirth.


If my barren spirit
had your fertility,
it would already have forged a heaven
to complete its world.


But tell me, what effort can there be
in a soul without a flag
that carries everywhere
your torturer—who knows?;


that lives fasting from faith
and, with tenacious heroism,
goes asking every abyss
and every night a why?


In every case, my thirst
for investigation shields me,
my deep and silent thirst for God;
and there is more love in my doubt
than in your tepid affirmation.

translation.title: The Shadow of the Wing
translation.editorial_note: The source punctuation around “tu torturador ¿quién sabe?” is syntactically irregular and remains marked in English.
